title: My Nephew Forged My Signature, Sold The Bikes, And Mailed Me $3,800. So I Voided The Sale
description: I spent 30 years as a hospital cafeteria worker and cashed out my $117,000 401(k) to open a vintage bicycle restoration shop with my nephew. He promised me 45 percent and free tune ups for my grandkids in writing, then forged a dissolution, sold the restored 1890s penny farthings and early roadsters to a museum for $620,000, and mailed me a $3,800 check labeled final settlement. I found our signed agreement inside a hollow seatpost on a 1937 Schwinn Autocycle, voided the sale, and now he trues wheels in an orange vest that says Spun Out of Trust. #RevengeStory #FamilyBetrayal #VintageBikes
thumb_text: HE SOLD MY BIKES FOR $620,000 AND MAILED ME $3,800
pinned_comment: After my nephew forged a dissolution, sold my restored penny farthings for $620,000, and mailed me a $3,800 'final settlement' check, what would you have done? Tell me if a family member ever tried to write you out of a deal, share your story in the comments.
